mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over the previous month signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a weakening labor market, which typically leads to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the previous two months signals increased demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where HOUST increases > 5% in the previous two months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a contraction in the supply side of the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of instances where INDPRO shows a decline.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the previous month, the combined effect of high interest rates and inflationary pressures typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by more than 0.3 percentage points and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) decline in the same month, the combined signal of a weakening labor market leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp and PAYEMS declines in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 70% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp and PAYEMS declines in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real final sales (RSAFS) combined with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals robust consumer demand and a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% and UNRATE declines in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where RSAFS increases > 1% and UNRATE declines in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) decreases by more than 0.25 percentage points in a month, it signals a loosening monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS decreases > 0.25pp in the previous month.
